knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Double Integral Using the Additivity Over a Rectangular Domain

question.:question/problem:
![A scaled rectangular partition with coordinate ticks and labeled regions.](images/partition-38a6b83bd96fdb6e2bd0.png)

The rectangle $R$ is partitioned into the labeled regions shown. Define

$$
f(x,y)=\begin{cases}x y&(x,y)\text{ in the interior of }B\\\frac{y}{x}&(x,y)\text{ in the interior of }A\\2 y&(x,y)\text{ in the interior of }C.\end{cases}
$$

Set $f=0$ on the region boundaries. Evaluate $\iint_R f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}A$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Match each formula to its coordinate rectangle:

$$
\begin{aligned}B&=(1,4)\times(1,2)\\A&=(1,2)\times(2,4)\\C&=(2,4)\times(2,4)\end{aligned}
$$

The interiors do not overlap, and the boundaries have area zero. Add the integrals over these rectangles.

On $B$, separate the coordinate factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\iint_{B}(x y)\,\mathrm{d}A\\&=\left(\int_{1}^{4}(x)\,\mathrm{d}x\right)\left(\int_{1}^{2}(y)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)\\&=\left[\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{1}^{4}\left[\frac{y^{2}}{2}\right]_{1}^{2}\\&=\left(\frac{\left(4\right)^{2}}{2}-\left(\frac{\left(1\right)^{2}}{2}\right)\right)\left(\frac{\left(2\right)^{2}}{2}-\left(\frac{\left(1\right)^{2}}{2}\right)\right)\\&=\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)=\frac{45}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

On $A$, separate the coordinate factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\iint_{A}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}A\\&=\left(\int_{1}^{2}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\right)\left(\int_{2}^{4}(y)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)\\&=\left[\ln{\left(x \right)}\right]_{1}^{2}\left[\frac{y^{2}}{2}\right]_{2}^{4}\\&=\left(\ln{\left(\left(2\right) \right)}-(\ln{\left(\left(1\right) \right)})\right)\left(\frac{\left(4\right)^{2}}{2}-\left(\frac{\left(2\right)^{2}}{2}\right)\right)\\&=\left(\ln{\left(2 \right)}\right)\left(6\right)=6 \ln{\left(2 \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

On $C$, separate the coordinate factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\iint_{C}(2 y)\,\mathrm{d}A\\&=\left(\int_{2}^{4}(1)\,\mathrm{d}x\right)\left(\int_{2}^{4}(2 y)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)\\&=\left[x\right]_{2}^{4}\left[y^{2}\right]_{2}^{4}\\&=\left(\left(4\right)-(\left(2\right))\right)\left(\left(4\right)^{2}-(\left(2\right)^{2})\right)\\&=\left(2\right)\left(12\right)=24\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_R f\,\mathrm{d}A&=\left(\frac{45}{4}\right)\\&\quad+\left(6 \ln{\left(2 \right)}\right)\\&\quad+\left(24\right)\\&=\boxed{6 \ln{\left(2 \right)} + \frac{141}{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

conversions: evaluate displayed primitives at their own endpoints
expand products and add signed contributions
error_recipes: omit y primitive denominator in region 3

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Double Integral Using the Additivity Over a Rectangular Domain

question.:question/problem:
![A scaled rectangular partition with coordinate ticks and labeled regions.](images/partition-9ffc418adab6eb703067.png)

The rectangle $R$ is partitioned into the labeled regions shown. Define

$$
f(x,y)=\begin{cases}- y&(x,y)\text{ in the interior of }C\\x y&(x,y)\text{ in the interior of }B\\\frac{y}{x}&(x,y)\text{ in the interior of }A.\end{cases}
$$

Set $f=0$ on the region boundaries. Evaluate $\iint_R f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}A$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Match each formula to its coordinate rectangle:

$$
\begin{aligned}C&=(1,4)\times(-1,1)\\B&=(1,3)\times(1,2)\\A&=(3,4)\times(1,2)\end{aligned}
$$

The interiors do not overlap, and the boundaries have area zero. Add the integrals over these rectangles.

On $C$, separate the coordinate factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\iint_{C}(- y)\,\mathrm{d}A\\&=\left(\int_{1}^{4}(1)\,\mathrm{d}x\right)\left(\int_{-1}^{1}(- y)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)\\&=\left[x\right]_{1}^{4}\left[- \frac{y^{2}}{2}\right]_{-1}^{1}\\&=\left(\left(4\right)-(\left(1\right))\right)\left(- \frac{\left(1\right)^{2}}{2}-\left(- \frac{\left(-1\right)^{2}}{2}\right)\right)\\&=\left(3\right)\left(0\right)=0\end{aligned}
$$

On $B$, separate the coordinate factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\iint_{B}(x y)\,\mathrm{d}A\\&=\left(\int_{1}^{3}(x)\,\mathrm{d}x\right)\left(\int_{1}^{2}(y)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)\\&=\left[\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{1}^{3}\left[\frac{y^{2}}{2}\right]_{1}^{2}\\&=\left(\frac{\left(3\right)^{2}}{2}-\left(\frac{\left(1\right)^{2}}{2}\right)\right)\left(\frac{\left(2\right)^{2}}{2}-\left(\frac{\left(1\right)^{2}}{2}\right)\right)\\&=\left(4\right)\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)=6\end{aligned}
$$

On $A$, separate the coordinate factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\iint_{A}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}A\\&=\left(\int_{3}^{4}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\right)\left(\int_{1}^{2}(y)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)\\&=\left[\ln{\left(x \right)}\right]_{3}^{4}\left[\frac{y^{2}}{2}\right]_{1}^{2}\\&=\left(\ln{\left(\left(4\right) \right)}-(\ln{\left(\left(3\right) \right)})\right)\left(\frac{\left(2\right)^{2}}{2}-\left(\frac{\left(1\right)^{2}}{2}\right)\right)\\&=\left(- \ln{\left(3 \right)} + 2 \ln{\left(2 \right)}\right)\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)=- \frac{3 \ln{\left(3 \right)}}{2} + 3 \ln{\left(2 \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\ln(4)=2\ln(2)$ is used to simplify the logarithmic endpoint value.

Add the signed contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_R f\,\mathrm{d}A&=\left(0\right)\\&\quad+\left(6\right)\\&\quad+\left(- \frac{3 \ln{\left(3 \right)}}{2} + 3 \ln{\left(2 \right)}\right)\\&=\boxed{- \frac{3 \ln{\left(3 \right)}}{2} + 3 \ln{\left(2 \right)} + 6}.\end{aligned}
$$

conversions: evaluate displayed primitives at their own endpoints
expand products and add signed contributions
error_recipes: add y endpoint values in region 3

question.:question/problem:
![A scaled rectangular partition with coordinate ticks and labeled regions.](images/partition-1a43d38b45861b09d0c2.png)

The rectangle $R$ is partitioned into the labeled regions shown. Define

$$
f(x,y)=\begin{cases}\frac{y}{x}&(x,y)\text{ in the interior of }A\\x y&(x,y)\text{ in the interior of }B\\- 2 y&(x,y)\text{ in the interior of }C.\end{cases}
$$

Set $f=0$ on the region boundaries. Evaluate $\iint_R f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}A$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Match each formula to its coordinate rectangle:

$$
\begin{aligned}A&=(1,4)\times(-2,0)\\B&=(1,3)\times(0,1)\\C&=(3,4)\times(0,1)\end{aligned}
$$

The interiors do not overlap, and the boundaries have area zero. Add the integrals over these rectangles.

On $A$, separate the coordinate factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\iint_{A}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}A\\&=\left(\int_{1}^{4}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\right)\left(\int_{-2}^{0}(y)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)\\&=\left[\ln{\left(x \right)}\right]_{1}^{4}\left[\frac{y^{2}}{2}\right]_{-2}^{0}\\&=\left(\ln{\left(\left(4\right) \right)}-(\ln{\left(\left(1\right) \right)})\right)\left(\frac{\left(0\right)^{2}}{2}-\left(\frac{\left(-2\right)^{2}}{2}\right)\right)\\&=\left(2 \ln{\left(2 \right)}\right)\left(-2\right)=- 4 \ln{\left(2 \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\ln(4)=2\ln(2)$ is used to simplify the logarithmic endpoint value.

On $B$, separate the coordinate factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\iint_{B}(x y)\,\mathrm{d}A\\&=\left(\int_{1}^{3}(x)\,\mathrm{d}x\right)\left(\int_{0}^{1}(y)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)\\&=\left[\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{1}^{3}\left[\frac{y^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{1}\\&=\left(\frac{\left(3\right)^{2}}{2}-\left(\frac{\left(1\right)^{2}}{2}\right)\right)\left(\frac{\left(1\right)^{2}}{2}-\left(\frac{\left(0\right)^{2}}{2}\right)\right)\\&=\left(4\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=2\end{aligned}
$$

On $C$, separate the coordinate factors:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\iint_{C}(- 2 y)\,\mathrm{d}A\\&=\left(\int_{3}^{4}(1)\,\mathrm{d}x\right)\left(\int_{0}^{1}(- 2 y)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)\\&=\left[x\right]_{3}^{4}\left[- y^{2}\right]_{0}^{1}\\&=\left(\left(4\right)-(\left(3\right))\right)\left(- \left(1\right)^{2}-(- \left(0\right)^{2})\right)\\&=\left(1\right)\left(-1\right)=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_R f\,\mathrm{d}A&=\left(- 4 \ln{\left(2 \right)}\right)\\&\quad+\left(2\right)\\&\quad+\left(-1\right)\\&=\boxed{1 - 4 \ln{\left(2 \right)}}.\end{aligned}
$$

conversions: evaluate displayed primitives at their own endpoints
expand products and add signed contributions
